findings.heading: Developing an app server
findings.proposition: The translation states that the output object re-runs the server logic function every time an input changes; the English says the output re-runs 'this function', meaning the render/plot call, not the whole server function.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader forms the wrong mental model of Shiny reactivity, believing the entire server function re-executes on every widget change, and so expects all server-side code (including the one-off setup they may put there) to run again on each input change.

findings.heading: Adding a download button
findings.proposition: The translation states that `content` holds the data to be saved locally; the English states that `content` holds a function that you would use to save data locally, which is what the adjacent chunk shows (`content = function(file) ggsave(...)`).
findings.reader_consequence: A reader may pass a data object to `content` instead of a saving function, and the download handler then fails.

findings.heading: Adding a download button
findings.proposition: The English instructs the reader to put the `file` argument in the position where the output file name is specified; the translation instead only asserts that the `content` function saves the output file to a specified location.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader does not learn where `file` must be placed inside the saving call, so when adapting the pattern to another writer (for example `rio::export()`) they may omit `file` as the destination and the download produces no usable file.

findings.heading: Developing an app server
findings.proposition: The translation adds the examples '(such as textInput or sliderInput)' as instances of reactive sources; the English names no example widgets at this point.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader is given specific widget examples that the English author did not select, which narrows the notion of a reactive source to two text/slider widgets rather than to all user inputs, including the `selectInput()` widgets this chapter actually uses.

findings.heading: Adding a facility selector
findings.proposition: The translation states that the third thing passed to a widget-update function is a new input object holding all the choices of the `selectInput()` being updated; the English states that you pass new versions of all parameters that `selectInput()` already accepts.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader concludes only the choices can be updated, and expects to pass one object rather than named `selectInput()` parameters, so they do not discover that `label`, `selected` and other arguments can also be updated at run time.

findings.heading: Loading data into our app
findings.proposition: The translation adds a parenthetical translator's gloss defining startup code as code placed outside the server logic function so that it runs only once; the English gives no definition at this point.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader receives a definition the English author did not write, and it is narrower than the English concept: startup code is code that runs once before the app starts, whether in global.R or at the top of app.R, not merely code positioned outside the server function.

findings.heading: Developing an app server
findings.proposition: The translation adds the instruction to type something in, replacing the English exclamation 'Talk about reactivity!' which issues no instruction.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader may try to type into the R console while the app is listening, where the console is blocked and accepts no input, and conclude that something is broken.

findings.heading: Basic file structures
findings.proposition: The translation states that sourcing additional .R files is mandatory for a large app; the English states only that we should do so if we have a larger app.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader treats a multi-file layout as a requirement rather than a recommendation, and may believe a large single-file app is invalid.

findings.heading: Developing an app server
findings.proposition: The translation states that the reader does not need to fully understand when execution starts in a Shiny app; the English states that the execution order is not fully necessary to understand when starting out with Shiny, which is a beginner-stage qualification about the order.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader takes the point as permanent rather than provisional and drops the topic of execution order entirely, so they do not revisit it when writing a larger app where the order matters.
